notes: Manufacturer's own product page + linked cut-sheet PDF (https://plurainc.com/files/downloads/signal-processing/datasheet/Avenue_P9400_cut_sheet_rev_A2.pdf) were used. The device is the "Avenue P9400-4K" test-signal/sync-pulse generator, originally an Ensemble Designs product (the cut-sheet is still Ensemble Designs-branded) that Plura now sells/hosts under its own site as "Plura P9400-4K" — treat this as a Plura-branded continuation of the Ensemble Designs Avenue line. It is a card-based module comprised of two "9400" modules locked together, occupying two slots in a 1RU or 3RU Avenue frame — it has NO standalone AC power connector (draws 20W via the frame backplane), so no power port is listed. The 4 SDI outputs are individually 3G-SDI (SMPTE 425M-5 Level A); when combined they form a Quad-Link 4K/UHD signal (Square Division or 2-Sample-Interleave) — grade sdi-3g reflects the physical connector rating, not the composite 4K signal. Each of the two internal 9400 modules also has several additional software-programmable BNC outputs (individually configurable as Color Black, Tri-Level Sync, AES, DARS, Word Clock, LTC, or VITC), but the exact physical count of these programmable BNCs is not stated in the public cut-sheet, so they were omitted rather than guessed — actual unit likely has more BNC ports than listed here. No RS-232/RS-422, Ethernet, USB, or analog/AES audio connectors are documented on the cut-sheet (audio/timecode are embedded/programmable-output based, not on dedicated physical jacks per the available docs). No rack-unit size applies since this is a two-slot card, not a standalone chassis.

ports.name: Ext Ref A
